name: More Island Events
description: Adds new island events, written by the owner, beside the game's own (more come in later versions). Three here: The Aspiring Adventurer -- a villager who loves to explore sees something glinting off the safe path. "Go investigate!" finds a pile of dirt, a stack of meat (food) or a golden chest of artifacts (tech points); half the time the adventurer gets home (with the find, or with a friend's help), half the time a trap leads to death (a grave) or a disappearance (no grave). "Stay on the safe path" brings them home 9 times in 10; otherwise they are lost: hurt, healed or disabled, a skilled survivalist, killed, gone, or they become a Heathen. The event is rare and separate: it never takes a share of the game's own draw (the stock island events' chances never change); after a natural island event, Story / Cheat Upgrades' separate rare roll may bring one of these events (or an Isola Grand Event Collection event) between two natural ones, never in trouble and never in place of a rescue, and Pick Island Event can pick it; it needs two villagers of 14 or more who are not nursing a baby and not a Heathen, the chief, the Retired Chief or another of the special roles the game's own picker skips, or a Reanimated spirit, and the adventurer and the friend who may come to help are drawn from them. The reward is a random amount from the smallest to the largest food or tech-point gain of the game's own island events (50 to 300 food for the meat, 500 to 3,000 tech points for the chest); with Island Events Scale With Population or With Stored Food and Tech Points ticked, the amount scales as that patch scales the game's own events. Deaths are the game's own ("Unknown causes", with a grave); a disappearance is logged as one in the Deaths log. The popups show the owner's text in pages that fit the screen (OK shows the next) -- with Scrolling Popups installed, one scrolling popup for the question and one for each answer's result; the effects wait for the page that tells them, and the Island Events log keeps one entry for each event. And The Remembrance Ceremony and The Rumblings (all five games; one popup each, OK only). The Remembrance Ceremony needs at least one grave and The Last Heathen done (every Heathen converted and the hovel fixed up): everyone joins in -- children, nursing mothers and fathers, everyone who believes -- each at the mausoleum, "Honoring the Dead" -- or, with "Memorial Actions Can Also Occur at the Heathen Hovel" installed, half of them at the old Heathen hovel instead, "Honoring the Dead" or "Reflecting" (half the time each), and the feast quietly uses 10 food for every villager (never below 0). The Rumblings needs every puzzle solved and a finished structure: an earthquake damages each of the three population huts, the clothing hut and the love shack (the nursery school is left out) one time in four (at least one always), each losing 10 to 100% of its building work; the builders must build it again (at 100% it is unbuilt again, as in a new village; an unbuilt one can be moved). Nobody is hurt; a village over its limit keeps everyone and has no new births until it is rebuilt. Each can come again. Pick Island Event lists each of these events and picks one whenever its own requirements hold (otherwise it says what the event needs). Off by default; part of Classic VV Difficulty; Owner's Defaults ticks it. **Needs Story / Cheat Upgrades (on by default), which runs the rare roll and Pick Island Event; ticking this ticks it.** **Unverified in play: the event has not been seen in a running game** (emulated on the stock executable). The companion is "VVFP More Island Events.dll", started by VVFP Startup.dll; nothing is saved by it.
behavior_changes: The event is rare and separate: it never takes a share of the game's own draw (the stock island events' chances never change); after a natural island event, Story / Cheat Upgrades' separate rare roll may bring one of these events (or an Isola Grand Event Collection event) between two natural ones, never in trouble and never in place of a rescue, and Pick Island Event can pick it. It can happen only while at least two villagers may go: 14 or more (280 age units), alive and present, not carrying a baby, and not a Heathen, the chief, the Retired Chief or another of the special roles the game's own picker skips, or a Reanimated spirit; the adventurer and the friend of ending A8 are drawn from them, the friend never the adventurer.

Choice A, "Go investigate!": the find 50% a pile of dirt, 25% meat (a food award: 50 to 300 food), 25% a golden chest (a tech award: 500 to 3,000 tech points); then 50% a surviving ending (after the dirt A7 or A9; after a find A1, A5 or A8, which give the reward) and 50% a deadly one (A2 and A4 die, the game's own death with cause -1 and a grave; A3 and A6 disappear, no body), each equally likely within its half.

Choice B, "Stay on the safe path": 90% home safe; 10% lost, then 1 in 6 each: the healers (1 in 3 each: dies; a full recovery; health set to 10-50 and running disliked), becomes a Heathen, the game's own conversion ("the Isolans' tribe" with Guardians of Isola, else "the heathens' tribe"), a survivalist (+20 to 30 in Farming, Building, Research or Healing, at most 100), dies under a fallen tree, dies at the bottom of a cliff, disappears.

The reward is drawn, each amount equally likely, from the game's smallest to its largest stock island-event gain of that kind (src/vv_aspiring_adventurer.py AWARD_RANGES), and goes through the game's own food or tech writer; with Island Events Scale With Population or With Stored Food and Tech Points ticked, the amount scales as that patch scales the game's own events. The effects wait for their own page (the page that ends the ending's text), and the event writes its own one Island Events log entry; a disappearance is told to the Cause of Death companion (VvfpCauseVanishedBy), so its Deaths log records it as one.

The owner's words, by translation key (the event's popup shows the player's language when a translation has them), are laid out in pages that fit the game's popup -- whole paragraphs, else whole sentences -- each shown in turn with OK.

The Remembrance Ceremony and The Rumblings (ceremony_core.inc, ceremony_games.inc): each in slot 0 only while it is due (t_list adds no entry), no site of its own; the game's own single-result popup shows the owner's words, the effects are made as it is built, with the event's one Island Events log entry. The Remembrance Ceremony: needs at least one grave and The Last Heathen done (every Heathen converted and the hovel fixed up) (the game's own grave count); every living, present villager who is a believer is started on its own through the game's own stop and action starter, as its Day of Honor starts each one (so no group filter leaves anyone out), at the mausoleum, "Honoring the Dead" -- or, with "Memorial Actions Can Also Occur at the Heathen Hovel" installed, half of them at the old Heathen hovel instead, "Honoring the Dead" or "Reflecting" (half the time each); the feast uses 10 food for every villager the game counts, never below 0 (Blessings Day's own rule). The Rumblings: needs every puzzle of the game's Puzzles screen solved and one of the three population huts, the clothing hut and the love shack (the nursery school is left out) finished; each finished one rand(100) < 25 (none: one of them at random), each losing 10 + rand(91) percent of its building work, written as the states the game's own construction passes through (at 100% the new village's state); the building's effect handle freed and set to -1; a damaged population hut's count of the still-locked "3 huts" trophy taken back (saved with the village at the state's +0x328), so it still needs three different huts.
explicit_non_changes: No executable byte is patched: the companion writes each site at run time, only after verifying every site's stock bytes (all of them, or none); without it the event does not exist.
Every stock event, its odds, the island-event timer and counting, the rescue rules and Custom Island Events are unchanged; nothing is saved by the companion.
